id_routing.description: Interconnect may append bits to AxID to identify the originating master; slave-side ID_WIDTH > master-side ID_WIDTH
id_routing.compliance_note: Returning ID is the WIDER value; routing strips appended bits before returning to the master

fields.topology_type: Two-wire current loop between an ECU and one or more sensors. Point-to-point (one sensor; PSI5-P variant), parallel bus (several sensors sharing the loop, each in its own time slot in synchronous mode), and daisy-chain (universal timing) topologies.

supported_topologies.name: Point-to-point
supported_topologies.description: One sensor on a dedicated two-wire current loop (PSI5-P variant).

supported_topologies.name: Parallel bus
supported_topologies.description: Several sensors share one two-wire current loop; in synchronous mode each transmits in its own time slot (time-division multiplexing).

supported_topologies.name: Daisy-chain (universal timing)
supported_topologies.description: Sensors connected in a daisy chain with the PSI5 universal timing model.

master_slave_role_summary.description: Powers the two-wire current loop, emits the sync pulse (synchronous mode), and senses/decodes the loop current.
Loop-powered transmitter; current-modulates its Manchester-coded telegram onto the loop in its time slot (synchronous) or autonomously (asynchronous).

fields.interconnect_role: PSI5 is a sensor<->ECU link, not a routed bus. Multiple sensors on a parallel bus are separated by time slots (time-division), not by addresses; the ECU is the loop master that powers the loop and (synchronously) triggers transmission.
fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: PSI5 has no address space; on a parallel bus, sensors are distinguished by their time slot relative to the ECU sync pulse.
